title: Finance & Legal: Integrated Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Policy
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
---
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's policies and standard procedures for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, contracts and legal review process, procurement approvals and vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition (RevRec) and billing practices. The goal is to provide a single reference for finance, legal, procurement requestors, and business owners so decisions are consistent, auditable, and compliant with accounting standards and our internal controls.

Scope and applicability
---
- Applies company-wide for all business units, products (Hosted, Dedicated, Private), and geographies unless otherwise noted.
- Excludes isolated customer-specific contractual clauses that are managed under the enterprise legal exceptions process (see Related Pages).
- Operational roles referenced: Requestor (business owner), Procurement Coordinator, Finance Approver, Legal Reviewer, VP/Director approvers, and Controller.

1) Budgeting and forecasting
---
Purpose: provide a consistent annual planning cadence with rolling quarterly forecasts and a mid-year reforecast process.

High-level cadence
1. Annual planning kickoff: November. Finance issues targets and planning templates to all departments.
2. Department submissions: December. Budget templates include headcount (FTEs), OPEX categories (cloud/GPU, SaaS, office), CAPEX, and anticipated contract renewals.
3. Executive review and consolidation: January. Finance runs validation pass and presents proposed plan to ELT.
4. Board approval: February (annual budget effective Mar 1).
5. Rolling forecast: updated monthly; deep reforecast in July (mid-year).

Planning standards and assumptions
- Currency: USD unless explicitly scoped to a local entity. FX impacts must be modeled separately.
- Headcount: hiring plans must include role, level, cost center, salary band, start date, and ramp profile.
- Cloud/GPU costs: product teams must provide usage baselines and any anticipated model onboarding impacts (e.g., new large-model inference queues).
- Contingency: 3% corporate reserve for unplanned expenses; program owners may request release with documented business case.

Approval matrix (summary)
| Amount (USD) | Required Approvals | Notes |
|--------------|--------------------|-------|
| <= 5,000 | Cost Center Owner | Routine purchases (SaaS seats, minor infra) |
| 5,001 - 50,000 | Cost Center Owner + Procurement Coordinator | Requires competitive sourcing for services > 25k if available |
| 50,001 - 250,000 | Department Head + Procurement + Finance Director | Strategic vendor review required |
| 250,001 - 1,000,000 | VP Finance + Legal + Procurement | Board notification for multiyear commitments |
| > 1,000,000 | CFO + CEO + Legal + Board approval | Multiregional or strategic commitments require board approval |

Budget change control
- Any budget reallocation > 10% of a line item or > $250k requires submission of a Budget Change Request (BCR) with justification, impact analysis, and signoffs per the matrix above.

2) Contracts and legal process
---
Objective: reduce negotiation cycle time while ensuring legal risk is managed and standardized terms are used where possible.

Contract lifecycle overview
1. Intake: Requestor submits the Contract Intake form (Confluence link and template). Include SOW (if applicable), start/end dates, pricing, and data handling requirements.
2. Triage: Legal triages for standard vs non-standard terms; Finance reviews for payment terms and budget alignment.
3. Standard templates: Use approved Redwood Master Services Agreement (MSA) or Purchase Order (PO) templates for typical vendor and customer contracts. Deviations create a Change Log entry.
4. Negotiation: Legal leads negotiations for terms of use, IP, confidentiality, liability caps, indemnities, data residency, and security obligations. Procurement supports vendor commercial terms.
5. Approval: Obtain approvals per the Approval Matrix. Legal issues an Approval Memo for non-standard terms.
6. Execution: Contracts executed via company e-signature platform. 
7. Post-execution: Contract metadata added to the Contract Registry and assigned to a contract owner for renewals and compliance checks.

Key review checklist (required items)
- Scope of services / deliverables and acceptance criteria
- Term and termination rights, including early termination fees
- Pricing, invoicing frequency, and payment terms (Net 30 default)
- Liability cap and indemnity language aligned with risk policy
- Data protection: SOC2, ISO certifications, encryption-at-rest, encryption-in-transit, and any Customer Data residency requirements
- Subcontracting and third-party dependencies
- Export controls and sanctions screening (global vendors)
- IP ownership and licensing for custom work

Special contract categories and handling
- NDAs: Standard NDA template; front-line sales/SE may sign using delegated NDA authority.
- MSA + SOW: Preferred for multi-deliverable relationships. SOW must include acceptance tests for software/feature delivery.
- Customer SaaS agreements: Legal to review all customer-facing terms, RTO/RPO SLAs, and security annexes.
- Complex/custody customers (e.g., regulated industries): Route through Security & Compliance review; may require Private deployment addendum.

3) Procurement procedures and vendor onboarding
---
Objectives: ensure competitive sourcing for material spend, manage vendor risk, and centralize vendor information.

Vendor selection and sourcing
- For purchases > $25k, Procurement must run a sourcing event or provide a documented single-source rationale.
- Use three bids where practical for software/services above $100k. Document comparisons in the Sourcing Summary.
- Preferred vendors list: Procurement maintains an approved vendor list for commonly used services (cloud, monitoring, legal counsel, payroll).

Vendor onboarding checklist
- Completed Vendor Onboarding Form with W9/W8 and bank details
- Insurance certificates (general liability, cyber liability where applicable) and tax forms
- Security questionnaire completed or SOC2 report provided for vendors handling customer data
- Sanctions and watchlist screening completed by Procurement
- Payment terms confirmed; Treasury records banking details for ACH/Wire setup

Procurement process (step-by-step)
1. Requestor completes Purchase Requisition in the procurement system and attaches Contract Intake if relevant.
2. Procurement validates budget availability and performs sourcing if required.
3. Procurement issues PO or routes contract to Legal for signature.
4. Vendor sends invoice citing PO or contract reference. Accounts Payable (AP) processes invoice per payment terms.

Escalation and exception handling
- Single-source or emergency procurements require a Procurement Exception form and signoff from Procurement Director and Finance Director.
- For disputes (delivery or pricing), open a Procurement Dispute ticket; Procurement and Legal will triage.

4) Revenue recognition (RevRec) and billing policies
---
Objective: align revenue recognition with ASC 606 principles (identify contract, performance obligations, transaction price, allocate price, recognize as performance obligations satisfied) and apply consistent billing practices.

Revenue recognition principles
- Subscription/hosted API revenue: recognized ratably over the service period once the customer has access to the service.
- Usage-based revenue (per-token, embeddings): recognized as the service is delivered (consumption period). Deferred revenue recorded at invoice when payment is received for future periods.
- Professional services / SOW: recognized upon satisfaction of performance obligations. If services are distinct and separately priced, recognize individually; if bundled, evaluate principal vs agent and allocate transaction price.
- Multi-element arrangements: allocate transaction price to each performance obligation based on standalone selling price estimates. Document assumptions and methodology.

Invoicing and billing cycles
- Standard customer billing: monthly in arrears for usage and monthly/quarterly in advance for subscriptions based on contract terms.
- Payment terms: Net 30 default for customers unless negotiated. Late fees: 1.5% monthly on overdue balances after 30 days unless otherwise negotiated.
- Credit and refunds: Credits are issued for invoicing errors, SLA credits (per contract), or approved customer disputes. Credits are recorded to revenue contra-accounts.

Revenue audit controls and reporting
- All customer contracts are logged in the Contract Registry and linked to the billing system.
- Revenue reconciliations: monthly close includes deferred revenue rollforward, recognized revenue, and unapplied cash.
- Internal monthly RevRec review: Finance, Accounting Manager, and Revenue Operations review material contract changes and judgment items.
- External audit support: maintain contract evidence, SOWs, invoices, change orders, approvals, and RevRec schedules for auditors.

Billing disputes and collections
- Minor disputes (< $5k): Customer Success & Revenue Ops manage and resolve within 15 business days.
- Material disputes (> $5k): Revenue Ops, Legal, and Finance coordinate; place suspense on further billing until resolution per contract terms.
- Collections: overdue balances escalate to Treasury and may be subject to hold or termination clauses in customer agreements.

5) Roles, responsibilities, and ownership
---
- Requestor (business owner): Submits intake forms, provides acceptance criteria, and ensures budget alignment.
- Procurement Coordinator: Executes sourcing, vendor onboarding, and maintains vendor master data.
- Legal: Contract review, risk assessment, and final approval for non-standard terms.
- Finance Approver / Director: Budget validation and financial signoff for approvals per matrix.
- Controller: RevRec oversight, accounting policy ownership, and audit liaison.
- VP/CFO: Executive approvals for large commitments and policy exceptions.

6) Controls, monitoring, and exceptions
---
- Quarterly compliance checks: Internal Audit or Finance runs a sample of contracts, procurements, and invoices for policy adherence.
- Contract registry health: target 100% of executed contracts logged within 5 business days of execution.
- KPI examples: average contract cycle time (target < 15 business days for standard contracts), procurement sourcing win-rate, days sales outstanding (DSO target < 45 days).
- Exceptions: documented via an Exceptions Log with business justification and required approvers depending on the magnitude of the exception.

Templates and resources
---
- Contract Intake Form (link to template)
- Master Services Agreement (MSA) and Standard NDA templates
- Budget template (xlsx), BCR template, and CapEx request form
- Vendor Onboarding Form and Security Questionnaire
- Revenue Recognition checklist and RevRec journal schedule template

Appendices
---
A. Glossary (selected)
- BCR: Budget Change Request
- MSA: Master Services Agreement
- SOW: Statement of Work
- RevRec: Revenue Recognition

B. Frequently asked questions
- Q: Who can sign NDAs?
  A: Sales/SE can sign the standard NDA using delegated authority; any changes to NDAs require Legal signoff.
- Q: What if a vendor cannot provide SOC2?
  A: Procurement & Security will perform a compensating controls risk assessment; high-risk handling of customer data typically requires SOC2 or equivalent.

Contact and escalation
---
For questions about policy interpretation, contact Finance Policy (finance-policy@redwood.ai) or Legal (legal-ops@redwood.ai). For urgent vendor or contract escalations, tag Procurement Director and Legal Lead.
